'''Karen Helen Wiltshire''' (born 1962) is an Irish and German Climate and [[Marine scientist|Marine Scientist]]. She is a Professor of Climate Science and E3 CRH Chair of Climate Science at Trinity College Dublin, as well as a Professor of [[shelf-ecosystem|Shelf-Ecosystem]]s at the [[Kiel University|University of Kiel]] in Germany. Karen was one of the first women in a Directorate of a [[Helmholtz Association|Helmholtz research center]] in Germany, becoming Vice Director of the [[Alfred Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research]] (AWI) 2006-2024.<ref name="R1">{{Cite web |title=Leitung |trans-title=Management |url=https://www.awi.de/ueber-uns/organisation/leitung.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706212808/http://www.awi.de/ueber-uns/organisation/leitung.html |archive-date=2015-07-06 |website=[[AWI.de]] |language=DE}}</ref>

Born in [[Dublin]], Wiltshire studied at [[Maynooth University]] and [[Trinity College Dublin]], graduating with a Master's degree in [[Environmental science]]. She received her PhD (1992) and Habilitation (2001) in [[Hydrobiology]] at the [[University of Hamburg]]. She has held leadership positions in several major international scientific institutions - {{ill|GKSS Geesthacht|de|GKSS-Forschungszentrum}}, the [[University of St Andrews|University of St. Andrews]], Scotland, [[University of Groningen]], Netherlands and the [[Max Planck Institute of Limnology]], Germany. She was appointed Professor of [[Geomicrobiology]] at [[Jacobs University]], Germany in 2006.<ref name="R2">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Karen Helen Wiltshire |url=https://www.awi.de/ueber-uns/organisation/mitarbeiter/karen-helen-wiltshire.html |website=[[AWI.de]] |language=DE}}</ref> In her research capacity, she contributed to the preservation of the North Sea "Helgoland Roads Time Series" data set, [https://www.nationalgeographic.com/environment/article/watching-the-sea-change-from-a-tiny-german-island by linking it to international databases and models showing marine ecosystem change due to climate and environmental factors].

Karen Wiltshire co-founded [[Scientists for Future]] in Germany, and was the first female chair of POGO [https://pogo-ocean.org/ (Partnership for Observations in the Global Oceans)].<ref name="R3">{{Cite web |date=12 March 2019 |title="Scientists for Future" zu den Protesten für mehr Klimaschutz – BPK vom 12. März 2019 |trans-title="Scientists for Future" on the protests for more climate protection – BPK from March 12, 2019 |url=http://www.jungundnaiv.de/2019/03/12/scientists-for-future-zu-den-protesten-fuer-mehr-klimaschutz-bpk-vom-12-maerz-2019/ |website=Jung & Naiv |language=DE}}</ref> She has helped shape national and international science policy contributing to [[UNEP]], [https://scor-int.org/work/groups/scor-ocean-carbon-working-groups/ SCOR-UNESCO], [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change|IPCC]], IIASA, [https://www.ices.dk/Pages/default.aspx ICES] and as a lead coordinating author for [https://www.grida.no/publications/507 GEO07 Ocean and Coasts].

Wiltshire co-founded the Ocean Training Partnership with POGO, as well as the All-Atlantic [https://allatlanticocean.org/atseanetwork/ Sea Network] for training early career ocean professionals. She was the Director of the [https://www.awi.de/en/about-us/sites/helgoland/guest-research/centre-of-excellence-nf-pogo/10-years-of-excellence.html NIPPON-POGO Centre for Excellence for Oceanography] for 10 Years.

In 2024, Wiltshire was appointed as the Professor of Climate Science in Trinity College Dublin and holds the [[CRH plc|CRH]] Chair of Climate Science.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dublin |first=Trinity College |title=Trinity welcomes Professor Karen Wiltshire as first CRH Chair of Climate Science - E3 {{!}} Trinity College Dublin |url=https://www.tcd.ie/e3/news/trinity-welcomes-professor-karen-wiltshire-as-first-crh-chair-of-climate-science/ |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=www.tcd.ie |language=en}}</ref>

In 2025, she was made a fellow of Trinity College Dublin.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tcd.ie/news_events/articles/2025/new-scholars-and-fellows-announced-at-trinity-/ |title=New Scholars and Fellows announced at Trinity |date=28 April 2025 |website=tcd.ie |publisher=Trinity College Dublin |access-date=2025-05-12}}</ref>

In November 2025 Karen Helen Wiltshire was awarded the international AG Huntsman Award (https://www.huntsmanaward.org/)  for Excellence in Marine Science. She was honoured for her research into the effects climate change on marine ecosystems, her initiation of Marine Shipboard training platforms (Pogo Ocean Training Partnership) and her international work on marine and climate policy.
